title: stabilize-chunk-latch-and-event-marshaller-to-prevent-mid-json-cutoffs
author: Marisol Vega
body:
Motivation: Intermittent production reports and e2e tests showed streaming responses occasionally cutting JSON objects mid-object when a large model token boundary aligned with transport chunking; downstream OpenAI-compatible clients and our function-call marshaller would drop trailing function arguments or emit malformed structured output. This PR introduces a lightweight chunk-latch and an event marshaller boundary guard to guarantee that emitted SSE events never split a JSON structural token (object/array/string) across a user-visible event boundary. Approach: 1) Add a chunk-latch in the stream emitter that defers flush of a packet if it would split a JSON structural token within the last N bytes; the latch is size- and time-bounded so it cannot block indefinitely. 2) Extend the event marshaller to annotate intermediate frames with minimal reassembly hints (four-byte ASCII markers) that are safe for OpenAI-compat consumers and ignored by existing parsers. 3) When function/tool call tokens are detected in the tokenizer stream, the marshaller escalates to an atomic emit window to ensure fncall sentinel and trailing JSON are co-emitted. 4) Add heuristics to prefer emitting trailing delimiter (

 or SSE "
") on the same event as an unfinished JSON value rather than emitting an incomplete value and a delimiter in the next event. 5) Preserve backward compatibility by making all new behaviors opt-in via runtime flag stream.chunk_latch_enabled=true and a compatibility shim for older clients. Testing: unit tests for chunk-latch behavior, property-based tests for random token boundary placements, integration tests with openai-compat shim, and a small canary deployment with dedicated traffic shaping. Rollout: feature gated and behind rollout policy; start with 1% of hosted streaming traffic, increase to 25% after 24 hours of stability checks, then to 100%. Related: ENG-2345 (stability incident), ENG-2401 (compat edgecases), references to existing SSE framing workitems. Impact: reduces partial JSON incidents and misordered fncall handoffs while keeping latency impact under 3ms p50 for common small-chunk workloads.
commits: Marisol Vega: introduce chunk-latch emitter and marshaller boundary guard (initial)
Refactor: move stream framing helpers into streaming/frame_utils.rs
Tests: add property tests for random split positions and fncall atomic windows
Docs: document stream.chunk_latch_enabled runtime flag and upgrade notes
Fix: compatibility shim for old openai-compat clients that ignore reassembly hints
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Looks good overall, nice safe default gating. Can you add a microbenchmark comparing p50/p95 latency with and without latch for 1-token and 256-token streams?

Marisol Vega: Added benchmark script and updated bench results in scripts/bench/stream-latch-bench.rs. p50 impact is ~1.8ms on our canary hardware and p95 is +3.9ms for pathological small-chunk cases.
Clara Nguyen: We should be careful about the ASCII hint colliding with valid payloads. Please confirm hint bytes are chosen from an unlikely range and documented in the compat shim.

Marisol Vega: Hint uses 0x1E 0x1E 0xF0 0xF1 pattern which is invalid UTF-8 when placed mid-UTF8 and we explicitly strip it in the compat shim for older clients. Documented in docs/streaming/chunk-latch.md.
Owen Martinez: Integration test failed once in CI due to a race in the latch timer; request a small change to make timer cancellation atomic.
Marisol Vega: Fixed by switching to a cancelable future and added a test that simulates timer cancelation under high load.
QA Bot: flake detected in property test run; reran and passed after timeout increased to 500ms for one assertion.
Security Team: reviewed compat shim, no secrets introduced, good to ship with feature flag.
ci_summary: workflow: streaming-ci.yml - property tests: pass (rerun flaky test)
release_notes: Fixes intermittent partial-JSON emission over SSE by introducing a bounded chunk-latch and event marshaller boundary guard; prevents loss of function-call arguments during streaming and improves OpenAI-compat structured output stability. Opt-in via runtime flag stream.chunk_latch_enabled.
upgrade_instructions: Operators should enable stream.chunk_latch_enabled on a staged rollout. Expect a small p50 latency increase on pathological tiny-chunk workloads; rollout canary and observe streaming.events.partial_json metric. Back out by disabling the runtime flag.
